title: Hyperlocal model landscape scouting & latency-affinity canvas
creator: Elena Garcia
description:
Purpose: produce a repeatable, prioritized canvas for 'hyperlocal' model scouting that ties competitive model signals to buyer latency-affinity and deployment-mode fit (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Goal is a single artifact the GTM/Product/Platform teams can use to: 1) rank emergent models by enterprise fit, 2) map expected latency/cost tradeoffs by region and hardware, and 3) recommend fallback policy families for high-value customers.

Scope: competitive model analysis (capabilities & constraints), regional latency profiling (NA/EU/APAC), early procurement signals (supplier SLAs, availability windows), and product recommendations (API surface tweaks, rollout priorities, pricing sensitivity probes). This ticket captures product-level synthesis and the concrete deliverables we need to ship to sales and infra: a ranked model canvas, a latency-affinity heatmap, and a recommended action list for model rollouts and fallback policies.

Why now: Recent vendor outages and rapid emergence of specialized, low-latency model flavors in APAC have increased customer sensitivity to region-specific latency and procurement risk. We need an operationalized way to convert model-scout signals into prescriptive product decisions (e.g., when to pin a customer to dedicated capacity vs accept hosted fallbacks).

Deliverables: 
- Ranked canvas (spreadsheet + one-pager) that scores models along: capability coverage, quantization friendliness, hardware affinity, regional provisioning risk, contract/SLAs, and expected per-token cost at target throughput.
- Latency-affinity heatmap (NA/EU/APAC) correlating observed 95th pct latency by seq-length with model quantization/profile recommendations.
- Fallback policy catalog linking customer tiers to acceptable model-variant substitutions and cost thresholds.
- One-sheeter for sales with recommended negotiation talking points and procurement triggers.

Data sources & artifacts:
- Benchmarks: internal perf lab runs (see deck link below) and field traces from runtime-telemetry dashboards (Tokens/Reqs/95p latency by model).
- Market signals: vendor availability feeds, public release notes, GitHub repos for open-models, and provider status pages.
- Interviews: two enterprise AE interviews (EU Payments and NA Search platform) and recordings in Drive.

Key trade-offs and hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Customers with sub-200ms UI latency tolerance should be steered to dedicated capacity or local quantized variants—this reduces churn for high-frequency endpoints but increases ops costs.
- Trade-off: Prioritizing low-latency dedicated support for a handful of models increases reserved GPU commitments and reduces flexibility to swap providers quickly.
- Hypothesis B: APAC edge emergence favors smaller-context, aggressively-quantized variants; our runtime must expose clear cost/quality deltas per-variant to sales.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Canvas produced and validated by two AE partners and Platform lead.
2) Heatmap populated with telemetry-backed latency points for at least 6 candidate models across NA/EU/APAC.
3) Fallback catalog contains <=3 substitution families and clear SLA/cost guidance.
4) One-sheeter accepted by Sales leadership for use in 3 pilot deals.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: Benchmarks may not reflect customer payload distributions. Mitigation: run 2-week field probe with sample customer payloads (see subtask).
- Risk: Vendor SLAs are opaque. Mitigation: escalate to Partnerships for procurement clarifications and add contractual maturity score to canvas.

Notes on scope boundaries: This ticket is product-led research + deliverable creation. It does NOT include changing runtime routing logic or implementing new autoscaling policies—those are separate engineering tickets (linked as dependencies). Recommended rollouts or UI flags will be proposed but implemented under runtime/console squads.

Success metrics (how we’ll evaluate): 
- Sales adoption: 3 deals in pilot that reference the one-sheeter and accept recommended fallback policies.
- Operational impact: 20% reduction in customer latency incidents for pilot customers after switching to recommended variants.
- Decision velocity: baseline time-to-choose fallback model reduced from 8 days to 48 hours for pilot cohort.
